info.title: NimVor panel API
info.description:
The NimVor panel API manages websites, databases, backups, SSL certificates, deployments and more
over HTTPS and JSON. Every endpoint uses the same services as the web interface, so validation,
plan limits, ownership scope, auditing and the agent's safety checks are the same.

**Authentication.** Create a token under *Profile → API tokens* (it is shown once) and send it as
`Authorization: Bearer nimvor_…`. A token acts with its owner's permissions and ownership scope (a hosting
customer only sees their own websites). A *read-only* token may only use `GET`. Tokens can expire and
be revoked. There are no cookies and no CSRF token.

**Responses.** Success: `{"success": true, "data": …}`. Failure: `{"success": false, "error": {"code", "message", …}}`
with `reason`/`action` (what went wrong and what to do) or `fields` (one message per invalid input).

**Long operations** answer `202 Accepted` with a `job_id`; poll `GET /jobs/{id}` until `done` is true.

**Limits.** 120 requests per minute per token (`429 rate_limited`). Select another managed server with the
`X-NimVor-Server` header.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Who the token belongs to and which server it acts on.

tags.name: Server
tags.description: System information and current metrics of a managed server.

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description: Background jobs. Long operations (backups, deployments) return a `job_id`; follow it here.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: Job results and alerts the token's user may see.

tags.name: Websites
tags.description: Create, inspect, enable, disable and delete websites. Changes are validated (`nginx -t`, `php-fpm -t`), applied and rolled back on failure, exactly as in the web interface.

tags.name: SSL
tags.description: HTTPS certificates for a website.

tags.name: Backups
tags.description: Website backups (files and databases), optionally encrypted.

tags.name: Deployments
tags.description: Deploy a website from its connected Git repository.

tags.name: Subdomains and redirects
tags.description:
Subdomains and addon domains of a website, and its redirects.

A subdomain (`blog.example.com`) or an addon domain (a different domain) is a website of its own, with its own document root, running as the same system account as its parent. They show in `GET /websites` too, and removing one is `DELETE /websites/{id}` with its id. Plan limits for subdomains, addon domains and websites apply. The web server configuration is checked before it is reloaded and a refused change is undone.

Redirects are exact-path redirects of one website (up to 100).

tags.name: Applications
tags.description:
The one-click application installer: WordPress, Laravel and the other applications the server offers.

Only applications the token's user may install are listed (a hosting customer sees what the provider made visible). An install creates the application's database and user in the same step, runs in the background and answers `202` with a `job_id` to follow with `GET /jobs/{id}`. Only one install into a folder can run at a time. Check what an install would do first with the `plan` endpoint, which changes nothing.

tags.name: Web protection
tags.description:
Per-website protection against abusive traffic: request-rate limits, an allow/deny list and a country restriction.

Each change is written to the website's web server configuration, checked and reloaded; if the server refuses it the change is undone. A suspended account's protection cannot be changed (`409`). The server-wide lists are an administrator tool and are not part of this API yet; the ModSecurity firewall is under *ModSecurity*.

tags.name: ModSecurity
tags.description:
The ModSecurity web application firewall. Server administrators set it up (on/off, the OWASP Core Rule Set, custom rules, installation, updates); a website's owner may switch the website between off, detection only and on, but cannot change rule vendors or single rules.

Every change is checked by the web server (`nginx -t`) and the previous configuration is kept when it refuses. Installation, updates and rollbacks run in the background and answer `202` with a `job_id`.

tags.name: Databases
tags.description: MySQL and MariaDB databases and their users.

tags.name: Database users
tags.description:
MySQL/MariaDB accounts and what they may do. A user is `name@host`: the same name with another host is another account with its own password.

Names use lower-case letters, digits and underscores; a hosting customer's names get their account name as a prefix. Passwords are generated by the server and returned **once**. The stored-password "reveal" of the web interface is not offered by the API.

tags.name: Users
tags.description:
Panel users: administrators, staff, resellers and hosting customers.

The rules of the web interface apply: nobody can hand out a role whose permissions they lack, the last active administrator cannot be removed, disabled or demoted, nobody can delete or disable their own account, and a reseller only sees and manages their own customers. Two-factor resets and role editing are not part of the API.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Hosting accounts: a customer (or reseller) login with its plan, hosting options and first website, created in one step, and what administrators do with them afterwards: suspend, resume, change plan, terminate.

tags.name: Plans
tags.description: Hosting plans (resource limits) that can be assigned to accounts.

tags.name: DNS zones
tags.description:
DNS zones this server answers for, with their settings, zone files and DNSSEC.

Every change is checked and loaded by the DNS server; if the server refuses the zone, nothing changes. A hosting customer only sees the zones of their own websites and can only create the zone of a website of theirs.

tags.name: DNS records
tags.description: The records of a zone. Each type has its own checks (IPv4/IPv6 syntax, host names, MX priority, SRV and CAA fields, TTL), a CNAME cannot sit next to other records of the same name, and a zone holds at most 2000 records.

tags.name: Email domains
tags.description:
Domains this server receives and sends email for, with their DKIM keys and the DNS records they need.

A hosting customer only reaches the email domains of their own websites; the plan's limits (mailboxes, quota per mailbox) apply as in the web interface.

tags.name: Mailboxes
tags.description: Mailboxes of an email domain. Passwords must be 10–128 characters (no colon) and meet the server's password policy; a generated password is returned once.

tags.name: Email aliases
tags.description: Addresses that forward to one or more other addresses, including a catch-all for every other address of the domain.

tags.name: Email filters
tags.description:
Mail filters and the auto-responder of a mailbox, and the routing of an email domain.

Filters run on delivery, in list order. A filter has conditions (all of them or any of them) and actions. The whole set is written to the mail server in one go, so a change is all or nothing. A customer only reaches the mailboxes of their own email domains.

tags.name: Mail server
tags.description:
Administration of the mail server for server administrators: the delivery queue, Postfix and Dovecot settings, a troubleshooter, delivery reports, greylisting and the outgoing sending limits per website account. Mailboxes, aliases and filters are under *Email*.

Postfix and Dovecot settings are checked by the mail server and the previous values come back if it refuses them. Every change is audited.

tags.name: Cron jobs
tags.description:
Scheduled commands of a website, run as the website's system account.

A change rewrites the server's cron file for the website, which is checked; if the server refuses it the change is undone. A website can have at most 200 jobs and the plan's cron limit applies. A suspended account's jobs do not run (their settings are kept).

tags.name: Workers
tags.description:
Background workers of a website: queue workers, Node.js and Python apps and other long-running processes, run by systemd as the website's system account (`nimvor-worker-<name>.service`) and restarted by the rules you set.

A change is written and started by the server; if it refuses it the change is undone. The plan's worker limit applies. The values of a worker's environment variables are never returned (their names are), because they often hold secrets.

tags.name: FTP and SFTP
tags.description:
FTP accounts and SFTP access of a website.

An FTP account is a virtual login named `<name>@<website domain>`, confined to one folder of its website; the FTP server uses TLS by default. A website can have at most 25 accounts and the plan's FTP limit applies. SFTP uses the website's own system account, chrooted to its folder; it is off until you enable it. The FTP server itself (install, ports, TLS) is configured by an administrator in the panel.

tags.name: Backup schedules
tags.description:
Automatic backups of a website. Schedules are set up by administrators only; an account whose plan does not include automatic backups neither sees the schedules nor the copies they make (`scheduled: true`), and gets `404` for them.

A schedule runs daily or weekly at a full hour (server time) and keeps the newest `retention` copies, deleting older completed ones.

tags.name: Firewall
tags.description:
The server's firewall (UFW or firewalld), its protections and the confirmation of changes. Needs the security permissions, which hosting customers do not have.

**Every change is guarded.** The agent applies it, then undoes it automatically after **two minutes** unless you confirm it with `POST /security/confirm`. So a rule that cuts you off heals itself: check that you can still reach the server, then confirm. The agent also refuses a change that would remove SSH or the panel's own port (`502`, with a `reason`). Only one change can wait at a time.

A rule is named by its `spec`, exactly as `GET /security/firewall` lists it.

tags.name: PHP settings
tags.description:
The PHP version, limits and `php.ini` directives of a PHP website.

A change writes the website's PHP-FPM pool, which is checked with `php-fpm -t` before it is reloaded; if the server refuses it the previous settings are restored. Process limits, hardening and the security profile are the administrator's: a hosting customer who sends them gets `422` naming the fields. The customer's own `php.ini` and `.user.ini` files are never changed by the API.

tags.name: Services
tags.description:
The server's services (web server, PHP-FPM, databases, mail, DNS, FTP, …) and NimVor's own.

Needs the services permissions, which hosting customers do not have. The agent controls only the services on its allowlist and never SSH; it refuses anything else (`502` with a `reason`). Every operation is audited.

**Restarting the web server or NimVor itself.** Nginx carries the panel and the agent and the panel restart a few seconds after they answer, so such a call answers `202` with `scheduled: true`, and the API may not answer for a moment afterwards.

get.summary: The token's user and the selected server
get.description: Use it to check a token. It needs no permission beyond a valid token.

200.description: The user, the token and the server it acts on.

role.description: The role name, for example `admin` or `customer`.

scope.description: `own`: only the user's own resources are visible.

get.description: Operating system, kernel, CPU, uptime and network interfaces, with the latest CPU, memory, disk, load and network sample.

get.summary: Status and log of a background job
get.description: Only jobs started by the token's user are visible. Poll until `done` is true, passing the returned `offset` to receive only new log lines.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `job_id` returned when the job was started.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Byte offset in the job log to read from.

200.description: The job and its log since `offset`.

post.description: Give `ids` or `all: true`. Needs a read/write token.

all.description: Mark every notification of this user.

200.description: How many were marked and how many remain unread.

get.description: The websites visible to the token (a hosting customer only sees their own).

post.description: Validated against the hosting plan's limits, written as an nginx site (and a PHP-FPM pool for `php`), checked with `nginx -t` / `php-fpm -t`, applied, and rolled back on failure.

php_version.description: One of the PHP versions installed on the server (for `php` websites).

proxy_pass.description: Required for `proxy`: where requests are forwarded.

system_user.description: The Linux account to run as (administrators; defaults to a name derived from the domain).

delete.description: Removes the web server configuration and the PHP-FPM pool. **Files and the Linux account are kept** unless you ask for them to be removed (the account is kept anyway while another website uses it).

parameters.name: remove_user
parameters.description: Also delete the Linux account (when no other website uses it).

200.description: Deleted; `warnings` lists what could not be cleaned up.

post.description: Serves the website again after it was disabled.
Stops serving the website; its files and data stay.

post.summary: Issue a Let's Encrypt certificate and turn HTTPS on
post.description: The domain (and aliases) must resolve to this server. The certificate is issued, installed, the web server configuration is checked and reloaded, and HTTP redirects to HTTPS. Renewal is automatic.

include_aliases.description: Cover the aliases in the same certificate.

staging.description: Use Let's Encrypt's test environment (the certificate is not trusted).

get.description: The settings and the installed certificate (read from the server). Use `POST /websites/{id}/ssl` to issue a free Let's Encrypt certificate.

delete.description: The website is served over plain HTTP again and the redirect and HSTS are removed. Add `?delete_certificate=1` to also delete a Let's Encrypt certificate from the server (a later `POST` issues a new one).

parameters.name: delete_certificate
parameters.description: Pass `1` to delete the Let's Encrypt certificate too.

post.description: Runs in the background: the response is `202` with a `job_id`; follow it with `GET /jobs/{id}`.

label.description: A note shown in the backup list.

post.summary: Deploy from the connected Git repository
post.description: Pulls the repository connected under the website's Deploy tab and runs its steps, in the background. `202` with a `job_id`.

Creates `<subdomain>.<website domain>` as a website of the same type and PHP version as its parent. With `dns: true` an `A` record for it is added to the parent's DNS zone (when the parent has one and the server's default address is set).

subdomain.description: The label before the parent domain; `www` is not allowed (it is an alias of the website itself).

dns.description: Also add an `A` record to the parent's DNS zone.

dns_record_added.description: For a subdomain created with `dns: true`: an `A` record was added to the parent's DNS zone. False when there is no zone or the record already existed (add it on the DNS endpoints).

post.description: Hosts another domain as a website of its own under the same system account. The domain must not be a subdomain of the parent (create it as a subdomain). Point the domain's DNS to this server separately.
Redirects one exact path. A path can have one redirect (delete it first to replace it) and a page cannot redirect to itself.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The redirect's path, exactly as the list shows it (URL-encode it).

get.summary: List the applications that can be installed
get.description: Grouped by category. `installer_enabled` is false when the provider turned the installer off (then the list is empty).

apps.name: WordPress
apps.description: The world's most popular blog and website builder.

get.description: Every install into the website, newest first, with its result. Running installs are brought up to date first.

get.summary: Check what an install would do
get.description: A dry run: the requirements, the changes and any conflicts, worked out by the server without changing anything. `409` when the application does not fit the website (for example a PHP application on a static website).

post.description: Creates a database and user for it, then installs it in the background. For WordPress (and applications built on it) a strong administrator password is generated and returned **once**. Which fields apply depends on the application: `title`, `admin_user` and `admin_email` for WordPress and the applications that create an administrator, `path` for applications that go in their own folder, `migrate` for Laravel. A folder that already has an install running answers `409`.

path.description: A new folder name for applications that do not install into the document root.

target_id.description: Install into one of this website's subdomains instead (its website id).

website_id.description: The website it is installed into.

admin_password.description: Only for applications that create an administrator. Shown once.

200.description: The limits and what an over-limit visitor gets.

status.description: What a visitor over a limit gets: 429, 503, or 444 (the connection is closed without an answer).

post.summary: Add or replace a request-rate limit
post.description: Visitors that make more than `rate` requests per `unit` from one address to the path get an error. A limit with the same `name` is replaced (`200`), a new one is added (`201`); a website can have at most 20.

put.summary: Set what an over-limit visitor gets
put.description: The same answer for all of the website's limits.

status.description: What a visitor over a limit gets: 429, 503, or 444 (the connection is closed without an answer).

patch.summary: Turn a limit on or off

get.description: Entries by address, browser or URL. An `allow` entry lets that visitor through even when another entry or the country restriction would refuse them.

status.description: What a refused visitor gets: 403, 404, or 444 (the connection is closed without an answer).

max.description: The most entries a website can have.

post.description: Adds the entry, or changes the action and note of the entry with the same kind and value. Returns the whole list.

status.description: What a refused visitor gets: 403, 404, or 444 (the connection is closed without an answer).

max.description: The most entries a website can have.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The entry's value, as the list shows it (URL-encode it).

status.description: What a refused visitor gets: 403, 404, or 444 (the connection is closed without an answer).

max.description: The most entries a website can have.

put.summary: Set what a refused visitor gets

status.description: What a refused visitor gets: 403, 404, or 444 (the connection is closed without an answer).

max.description: The most entries a website can have.

post.description: One entry per line, in the form `deny ip 203.0.113.0/24  # note`. `merge` adds to the list (an entry with the same kind and value is changed); `replace` makes the text the whole list.

example.text:
deny ip 203.0.113.0/24  # scanner
deny ua BadBot

status.description: What a refused visitor gets: 403, 404, or 444 (the connection is closed without an answer).

max.description: The most entries a website can have.

put.description: Refuses the selected countries (`deny`), serves only them (`allow_only`) or turns the restriction off (`off`). It needs the country address database, which an administrator loads; without it the answer is `409`. Entries of the allow/deny list with `allow` still get through. **`allow_only` with the wrong countries locks real visitors out.**

codes.description: ISO two-letter country codes; required unless `mode` is `off`.

get.description: Whether it is on and loaded, the Nginx connector's state, the Core Rule Set and the custom rules. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

patch.description: Only what is sent changes. Turning it on needs the connector to be installed and usable. With `detection_only`, websites set to block only log until blocking is allowed. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

get.description: `enabled` says whether the server-wide "custom rules" switch is on; `next_id` is a free rule id. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

post.description: The whole set is checked by Nginx; nothing changes when it refuses. The rules file is at most 64 KiB. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

put.description: Send the `sha256` you read; if the rule changed meanwhile the answer is `409`. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

delete.description: Pass the rule's `sha256` as a query parameter. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

get.description: Requests ModSecurity logged or blocked, newest first. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

post.description: Runs in the background. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

post.summary: Install or upgrade the Nginx connector
post.description: A transaction on the server: everything is backed up first and rolled back if a step fails. `method`: `auto` uses packages where possible, `source` builds the connector. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

nginx_source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the Nginx source, for `source`.

post.summary: Install the OWASP Core Rule Set
post.description: It starts in detection only. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

get.description: Installation records, newest first, each with an `id` you can roll back. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

post.description: Runs in the background; nothing changes if Nginx would not accept the result. Server administrators only (`403` for others).

get.description: `mode` is `off`, `detect` (log only) or `on` (block attacks). `available` is false when ModSecurity is not loaded on the server.

put.description: Everyone who manages the website sets `mode`. `vendors_off` (`crs`, `custom`) and `disabled_rules` (up to 200 rule ids) are for server administrators; others get `422`. Only what is sent changes.

200.description: The databases visible to the token.

post.summary: Create a database, optionally with a user
post.description: Hosting customers' names get their account prefix. When `create_user` is true a user with all privileges on this database is created and **its generated password is returned once**, in this response only (unless `store_password` keeps it encrypted in the panel).

website_id.description: Link the database to one of the token's websites.

create_user.description: Also create a user with all privileges on it.

username.description: The user's name (default: derived from the database name).

store_password.description: Keep the generated password, encrypted, so it can be shown in the panel later.

201.description: Created. `user` and `password` are present only when a user was created.

get.description: One database with the users that may use it.

delete.description: **This deletes all the data in the database and cannot be undone** (take a dump first). Send the database's name as `confirm` (query string or body). The users that had access are kept.

post.summary: Dump a database to a file
post.description: Writes a SQL dump of the database to the server's backup directory, in the background. Returns `202` with a `job_id`: follow it with `GET /jobs/{id}`.

put.summary: Set what a user may do in a database
put.description: Gives the user access to the database, changes the access it has, or with `none` takes it away. `readwrite` is everything except `GRANT`; `all` includes it.

get.description: The users visible to the token (a hosting customer only sees their own), with the databases each may use.

post.description: Creates the account with a generated password (returned once). It has no access yet: give it some with `PUT /databases/{id}/grants/{user}`. To create a database together with a user, use `POST /databases` with `create_user`.

username.description: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, up to 32 (a hosting customer's account prefix counts).

website_id.description: Link the user to one of the token user's websites.

store_password.description: Keep an encrypted copy so it can be shown in the web interface.

host.description: Where the user may connect from: `localhost` (this server only), an IP address, a network with `%` such as `203.0.113.%`, or `%` (any host). Administrators may also use host names. A hosting provider can restrict customers to `localhost`.

password.description: The generated password. It is shown once and cannot be read again.

delete.description: Removes this account (`name@host`) and its access to every database. The databases and their data stay. Other hosts of the same name are other accounts.

post.description: Generates a new password and returns it once. Whatever uses the old one stops working.

store_password.description: Keep an encrypted copy so it can be shown in the web interface.

post.summary: Let a database user connect from another host
post.description: Creates a second account with the same name for the new host, with **its own new password** (returned once) and the same access to the same databases as this one. Opening a database to other hosts also needs the server's firewall to allow the database port.

host.description: Where the user may connect from: `localhost` (this server only), an IP address, a network with `%` such as `203.0.113.%`, or `%` (any host). Administrators may also use host names. A hosting provider can restrict customers to `localhost`.

get.description: Everyone for administrators and staff; a reseller sees only their own customers.

post.description: For a full hosting account with a website, use `POST /accounts`. A reseller can only create hosting customers, within their plan's customer limit. The generated password is returned once.

username.description: 3–32 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, starting with a letter.

role_id.description: A role whose permissions you hold yourself.

password.description: Must pass the password policy. Omit when `generate_password` is true.

generate_password.description: Create a strong password and return it once in the response.

201.description: Created. `password` is set only when it was generated.

patch.description: Only the fields you send change. Changing a password signs the user out of other sessions. Changing the role needs a role whose permissions you hold, and the last active administrator cannot be demoted or disabled.

password.description: A new password; must pass the password policy.

delete.description: Removes the panel login only. For a hosting account with websites, mail and databases use `POST /users/{id}/terminate`. You cannot delete yourself or the last active administrator.

post.description: In one step: the customer (or reseller) login, its plan and hosting options, and, when `domain` is given, its first website run by a new system account of the same name, with its DNS zone, mail and automatic SSL. If the website cannot be created the login is removed again.

username.description: Also the name of the website's system account.

password.description: Must pass the password policy. Omit when `generate_password` is true.

generate_password.description: Create a strong password and return it once.

domain.description: The first website's domain. Omit to create the login only.

php_version.description: PHP version of the website (default: the server's default).

reseller.description: Create a reseller instead of a customer (administrators only).

dns_dkim.description: Hosting option: publish DKIM in the website's DNS zone.

dns_dmarc.description: Hosting option: publish DMARC (needs DKIM and SPF).

spam_filter.description: Hosting option: filter the account's mail for spam.

spam_box.description: Hosting option: deliver spam to a Spam folder.

201.description: The account, its first website (when a domain was given) and the generated password (once).

post.description: Administrators only. The account cannot sign in; its websites, email logins, databases, FTP/SFTP, cron jobs and workers are turned off. **Nothing is deleted.** Suspending a reseller suspends their customers too. Repeat the call to retry parts that failed (`warnings`).

reason.description: A note kept with the account.

200.description: The account, suspended. `warnings` lists services that could not be turned off yet.

post.description: Administrators only. Turns the account's services back on.

put.description: The new limits apply from now on; nothing is removed. CPU, memory and other resource limits are applied at once (`warnings` says if that has to wait for the scheduler).

200.description: The account and its new plan.

post.description: **Destructive and not reversible.** Administrators only. Deletes the account's websites with their files and system accounts, mail domains and mailboxes, databases and DNS zones, then the login. A reseller can only be terminated after all of their customers. To guard against mistakes the request must contain `"confirm": "TERMINATE"`. Take a backup first (`POST /websites/{id}/backups`).

data.message: Terminated: 1 website(s), 3 mailbox(es), 1 database(s), 1 DNS zone(s).

get.description: The plans the token may assign: all of them for administrators, a reseller's own plans for a reseller.

200.description: The zones visible to the token, by name.

post.description: The zone gets the name servers set under Settings → DNS (an administrator sets them). With `template` it also gets the usual records: the address and `www`, SPF, optionally DMARC, and a CAA record for Let's Encrypt. Customers can only create the zone of one of their own websites (`website_id`), under the website's own domain.

name.description: The domain. Optional when `website_id` is given (the website's domain is used).

website_id.description: The website the zone belongs to.

template.description: Add the usual records (address, `www`, SPF, CAA).

warnings.description: Problems the zone has (for example a missing address for a name server); an empty list when it looks fine.

200.description: The zone, with any warnings about it.

warnings.description: Problems the zone has (for example a missing address for a name server); an empty list when it looks fine.

patch.description: The default TTL and the secondary servers allowed to transfer the zone. Only the fields you send change.

secondaries.description: IP addresses; an empty list allows none.

warnings.description: Problems the zone has (for example a missing address for a name server); an empty list when it looks fine.

delete.description: **The domain stops resolving from this server.** Give the zone's name as `confirm`.

post.description: Sends the whole zone to the DNS server again (for example after the DNS server was reinstalled).

warnings.description: Problems the zone has (for example a missing address for a name server); an empty list when it looks fine.

get.description: The zone as the DNS server serves it, in BIND zone file format.

post.description: Adds the records of a BIND zone file that are not in the zone yet. The SOA record, lines that are not supported, and records the zone could not hold (a CNAME next to other records) are skipped and listed in `skipped`; the zone's own name servers stay as they are. Up to 1 MB.

200.description: The records: the zone's `@` records first, then by name and type.

post.description: Checked for its type, added, and the zone reloaded; nothing changes when the DNS server refuses the zone.

name.description: `@` for the zone itself, or a name such as `www`, `mail`, `*.dev` (relative to the zone).

value.description: By type: an IPv4 address (A), an IPv6 address (AAAA), a host name (CNAME, NS, PTR, MX target, SRV target; a name that does not end in a dot is relative to the zone, `@` is the zone itself), text (TXT; one line, up to 4000 characters), `<flag> <tag> <value>` or `<tag> <value>` (CAA, for example `issue letsencrypt.org`).

installed_versions.description: PHP versions with PHP-FPM installed on this server.

php_version.description: One of `installed_versions`. Changing it moves the website to that version's PHP-FPM.

upload_max_mb.description: The largest upload (`upload_max_filesize`, `post_max_size` and the web server's body limit).

php_profile.description: The security profile, which decides the functions that are disabled. `custom` uses `disable_functions`. Administrators only.

disable_functions.description: With the `custom` profile: PHP functions to disable, separated by commas. Administrators only.

max_children.description: The most PHP processes the website may run at once. Administrators only.

pm.description: The PHP-FPM process manager. Administrators only.

start_servers.description: For `dynamic`; 0 lets the server choose. Administrators only.

min_spare_servers.description: For `dynamic`; 0 lets the server choose. Administrators only.

max_spare_servers.description: For `dynamic`; 0 lets the server choose. Administrators only.

idle_timeout_seconds.description: For `ondemand`: seconds before an idle process stops. Administrators only.

max_requests.description: Requests a process serves before it is replaced. Administrators only.

request_timeout_seconds.description: Stops a request after this long; 0 means no limit. Administrators only.

slowlog_seconds.description: Requests slower than this are written to the slow log. Administrators only.

harden.description: Extra hardening of the PHP pool. Administrators only.

lock_ini.description: Pin the plan's PHP limits so a `php.ini` or `.user.ini` cannot change them. Administrators only.

ini.description: The website's own `php.ini` directives, as `name: value`. **Replaces the whole set** (send `{}` to clear it, or use `DELETE …/php/ini`). Only the directives of the panel's list are accepted; paths must lie inside the website's folder.

owner_id.description: The reseller who owns the plan; null for the administrators' plans.

limits.description: Resource limits by name (`max_websites`, `max_databases`, `max_email_accounts`, `disk_quota_mb`, …); 0 means unlimited.

from.description: The path to redirect, starting with `/` (letters, digits and `. _ ~ - /`).

to.description: A full address (`https://example.com/new`) or a path (`/new`).

password_login.description: Whether a password is accepted besides keys.

keys.description: Authorized public keys, one per entry.

root.description: The folder that holds the websites; a website's files are under `<root>/<domain>`.

https.description: Whether the website is served over HTTPS.

mode.description: `letsencrypt` renews automatically; `custom` is an uploaded certificate that you renew yourself.

force_https.description: HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.

hsts.description: The HSTS header is sent (only with `force_https`).

security_headers.description: The standard security headers are added.

state.description: `expiring` means the certificate is within the server's warning period (14 days by default). Null without a certificate.

certificate.description: The installed certificate, read from the server. Null without HTTPS.

auto_renewal.description: Whether the server's renewal timer is active. Null for an uploaded certificate.

name.description: Identifies the limit; sending a limit with an existing name replaces it.

match.description: `prefix`: the path and everything below it; `exact`: that one address.

rate.description: Requests allowed from one address: up to 1000 per second or 60000 per minute.

burst.description: Extra requests tolerated in a burst before the limit bites.

per_ua.description: Count each browser (User-Agent) of an address separately.

enabled.description: False keeps the limit but does not apply it.

name.description: For example `admin`, `operator`, `viewer`, `reseller`, `customer`, or a custom role.

scope.description: `own`: the user only sees their own resources (a hosting account).

is_active.description: False: the user cannot sign in.

suspended.description: The account (or its reseller) is suspended: its services are off.

parent_id.description: The reseller this customer belongs to.

aliases.description: Other host names served by the same website.

kind.description: `php`: PHP-FPM; `static`: files only; `proxy`: reverse proxy to an application.

system_user.description: The Linux account the website runs as.

https.description: True once a certificate is installed and HTTPS is on.

owner_id.description: The panel user who owns it.

env_keys.description: Names of the variables set (not their values).

state.description: What systemd reports now; null when the server cannot say.

running.description: At least one copy is up.

command.description: One line, run from `directory` as the website's system account.

directory.description: A folder inside the website the command runs from; empty means the website's folder.

runtime.description: `node:<version>` or `python:<version>` of an installed runtime; empty or `system` uses the server's own.

memory_mb.description: Memory limit per copy; 0 means none.

enabled.description: False stops the worker; it stays in the list. A suspended account's workers stay stopped.

reason.description: Why (technical detail, also in the panel log).

fields.description: Input name → what is wrong with it.

Unauthorized.description: The token is missing, wrong, expired or revoked.

error.message: A valid API token is required (Authorization: Bearer nimvor_…).

Forbidden.description: The token may not do this: it is read-only, or its user lacks the permission or the hosting plan lacks the feature.

error.message: The token's user lacks the permission websites.manage.

NotFound.description: It does not exist, or it is not visible to this token.

error.message: Not found, or not visible to this token.

Conflict.description: The change was refused (for example a limit, a name already in use or a safety check); `reason` and `action` say why and what to do.

error.message: This domain is already used by another website.

ValidationFailed.description: An input is invalid; `fields` names each one.

RateLimited.description: More than 120 requests in a minute with this token.

error.message: Too many requests; at most 120 per minute per token.

AgentError.description: The server could not carry the change out (the agent refused it or is unavailable). Nothing was changed.

error.message: The web server configuration was not applied.
